cards.text: The LORD just sent Jeremiah, His prophet, to the gate of the LORD's house to tell the people of Judah to correct their ways (Jeremiah 7:2-3). Now the LORD turns to Jeremiah himself. And friend, this is NOT a pep talk.

cards.question: The LORD tells Jeremiah there's one thing he must not do for these people. What is it?
If Jeremiah begs the LORD for these people anyway, the LORD says He will still listen.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks Jeremiah if he sees what's going on in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. The sons gather wood, and the fathers light the fire.

cards.question: In the streets of Jerusalem, the sons gather wood and the fathers light the fire. What are the women making?

answers.text: Cakes for the Queen of Heaven
A cake for the prophet Elijah

cards.text: The whole family's on the dough, and on top of that, they pour out drink offerings to other gods. That's a family baking day, friend, for the WRONG party.

cards.question: The people also pour out drink offerings to other gods. Why, according to the LORD?
The LORD asks if He's really the One they're provoking, then says it's themselves they spite, to their own shame.

cards.text: Therefore the Lord GOD says His anger and fury will be poured out on this place. Man and beast, the trees of the field, the produce of the land. All of it.

cards.question: The LORD says His anger poured out on this place will burn and not be put out.

cards.text: A burnt offering normally goes up in smoke on the altar, all of it (Leviticus 1:9). But now the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, tells the people to add their burnt offerings to their other sacrifices.

cards.question: What does the LORD of Hosts tell the people to do with the meat from their sacrifices?
When the LORD brought their fathers out of Egypt, He gave more than rules about sacrifices. He commanded them to obey Him, and He would be their ___ and they would be His ___.

cards.text: And they were to walk in all the ways He commanded, so that it would go well with them. That was the deal from the start, friend.
The LORD is still speaking to Jeremiah about His people. Their fathers did not listen or incline their ear. They followed the stubborn inclinations of their own evil hearts.

cards.question: Instead of walking in the LORD's ways, the fathers who came out of Egypt went ___ and not ___.

cards.text: Backward, like a car stuck in reverse with the gas FLOORED. And from the day their fathers came out of Egypt until this day, the LORD has sent His servants the prophets.

cards.question: From the day their fathers came out of Egypt until this day, the LORD has sent His servants the prophets. How often?

cards.text: That's not one ignored text, friend. That's GENERATIONS of left on read.

cards.question: The people stiffened their necks, but the LORD says they did less evil than their fathers.
The LORD tells Jeremiah what will happen when he tells the people all these things. What will they do?

answers.text: Ask him to pray for them

cards.text: Therefore Jeremiah gets a message to say anyway: this is the nation that would not listen to the voice of the LORD their God and would not receive correction.

cards.question: Jeremiah is to say that ___ has perished and disappeared from their lips.

cards.text: Then the message turns to mourning: "Cut off your hair and throw it away."

cards.question: Jeremiah's message tells them to raise a lament on the barren heights. Why?

answers.text: The LORD has rejected that generation
Their king has been killed in battle
Their fields have all dried up

cards.text: The LORD goes on. The people of Judah have done evil in His sight, and they've set up their abominations in the house that bears His Name.

cards.question: The people set up their abominations in the house that bears the LORD's Name. By doing that, they ___ it.

cards.text: Friend, this is the hardest line in the passage. They built the high places of Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom so they could burn their sons and daughters in the fire.

cards.question: The LORD says burning their sons and daughters was something He commanded.

cards.text: So the days are coming, the LORD says, when that place won't be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom anymore. They'll bury the dead in Topheth until there's no more room.

cards.question: Topheth and the Valley of Ben-hinnom will be so full of the dead that they get a new name. What will they be called?

cards.text: And the corpses of this people will become food for the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth.

cards.question: When the birds and beasts come for the corpses, someone will be there to scare them away.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He'll remove the sounds of joy and gladness from the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, even the voices of the bride and bridegroom.

cards.question: The LORD will remove the sounds of joy and gladness, and even the voices of the bride and bridegroom, from Judah's cities. Why?

answers.text: The land will become a wasteland
The king will forbid all weddings
The prophets will call a fast

cards.text: And at that time, the bones of Judah's kings, officials, priests and prophets, and of the people of Jerusalem, will be removed from their graves.

cards.question: Those bones will be exposed to the sun and moon and all the host of heaven. What does the LORD say the people did with those?
After being dug up, the bones will be gathered up and buried again.

cards.text: Instead, they'll become like dung lying on the ground.

cards.question: Wherever the LORD has banished them, the remnant of this evil family will choose ___ over life.

findings.problem: Jeremiah 7:19 asks a rhetorical question: 'Is it not themselves they spite, to their own shame?' The card says the LORD 'then says' it's themselves they spite. That turns His question into a statement.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This story card is three sentences ('Therefore the Lord GOD says...' / 'Man and beast, the trees of the field, the produce of the land.' / 'All of it.'). It isn't the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong words 'guest', 'strangers' and 'rivals' don't fit the sentence. 'He would be their strangers' and 'He would be their rivals' aren't even grammatical, and 'their guest' sounds silly. That makes 'God' and 'people' stand out at once.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Card 3 and the question both say the LORD sent 'His servants the prophets', plural, from the day they left Egypt 'until this day'. That rules out the wrong answer 'Only once' before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke reacting to card 4. It tells no new part of the passage. It also cites Jeremiah 7:25-26 even though it tells nothing from 7:26.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card cites Jeremiah 7:25-26, but it tells no content from either verse.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This blank asks the baker to guess the wording of the line 'Truth has perished.' No earlier card mentions lying or speech, so nothing helps the baker reason toward 'Truth' over 'Wisdom' or 'Kindness'.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Most of the story cards in stop 3 (cards 7, 9, 11 and 14) are plain paraphrase with none of Papa Dorin's voice. The weight of the passage rules out jokes here, but his voice could still carry these moments.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Stop 2 card 1 is three sentences. It works like an opening card ('The LORD is still speaking to Jeremiah about His people.'). The 3-sentence allowance is written for 'the opening card', and the docs don't say whether that means only the passage's first card or the first card of each stop.
findings.question: Does the first card of each stop get the opening card's 3-sentence allowance, or only the first card of the whole walkthrough?
